target_profile.system_boundary: EPaxos replica implementation (swiftpaxos 'epaxos' package) coordinating a replicated state machine over intra-replica RPC.
protocol_contexts: EPaxos (corrected): per-replica instance rows keyed by (replica, instance); every replica may be a leader for its own row.
Thrifty fast path is mandatory in this build (recovery is incorrect without it, per source comment).
external_interfaces: fastrpc message handlers: Prepare/PrepareReply, PreAccept/PreAcceptReply, Accept/AcceptReply, Commit, TryPreAccept/TryPreAcceptReply
Client contract: defs.GPropose on ProposeChan and defs.ProposeReplyTS replies
ownership: InstanceSpace[replica][instance] is the slot for the row-owner replica; a coordinator (LeaderId) drives one instance.
Per-instance LeaderBookkeeping (lb) is held by the coordinator that is currently driving the instance.
variants: N<=3 thrifty special-case skips equality checking
N>7 propagates committed dependencies and requires allCommitted before fast commit
unknowns: Membership/Alive changes (A4) and quorum-file selection semantics are not yet read.
Durable stable-store format and recovery-on-restart replay path are not yet read (A6).

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement of a per-instance value.
activities.realization_summary: A coordinator pre-accepts a command, gathers a fast quorum of PreAcceptReply, and either fast-commits (allEqual + isInitialBallot + optionally allCommitted) or falls back to an Accept phase requiring a majority.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition/transfer of authority (ballot) for an instance.
activities.realization_summary: Each instance carries bal/vbal. A coordinator that loses the fast path or observes a higher ballot raises its ballot (makeBallot) and drives a recovery Prepare; acceptors adopt higher ballots and report their stored pre-accept state.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation for instances that cannot advance.
activities.realization_summary: executeCommands detects a stalled instance after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD and enqueues instancesToRecover; startRecoveryForInstance issues Prepare; the coordinator reconstructs state and either accept-commits, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase1.
executeCommands runs committed instances in dependency order using Tarjan SCC; strongconnect requires all dependencies committed and orders an SCC by Seq then owner then proposeTime.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support.
activities.realization_summary: recordInstanceMetadata/recordCommands/sync persist metadata and commands when Durable; not yet traced for replay on restart.
unknowns: Restart replay and checkpoint handling are not yet read.

The reply-to-request identity is recorded as F-CLIENT-REPLY-LINK and its unchecked consumption as B-CLIENT-OBSERVE.

formation.explanation: A coordinator pre-accepts a batch in its own row (B-PROPOSE/B-PHASE1), then aggregates PreAcceptReply: if the fast quorum agrees on seq/deps (allEqual), the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (for N>7) all committed deps are present, it fast-commits; otherwise it enters Accept and needs a majority. Both paths produce a concrete per-instance (Cmds, Seq, Deps) recorded as F-DECISION/F-COMMITTED and propagated by Commit.

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

open_details: CommittedUpTo is reported as PreAcceptReply.CommittedDeps and merged only when N>7; for smaller N the coordinator relies on local CommittedUpTo. Whether this is sufficient is a local question, not a formation gap.
handlePreAccept's Status>=ACCEPTED & Cmds==nil branch targets InstanceSpace[LeaderId][Instance]; unresolved whether LeaderId != Replica is reachable there.
findPreAcceptConflicts iterates from ExecedUpTo[row] (not +1); whether an already-executed instance can be misclassified as a conflict is a local anomaly.
core_overview.rationale: Both core lines are traced from proposal through aggregation, decision, propagation to execution, and the ballot-based authority transition that connects recovery to formation. Remaining items are local anomalies rather than unexplained formation, authority transition, or old-work handling.
